sources.entry: AI Monitor - Companion app that shows Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, and Cursor usage limits on a USB-connected ESP32 desk display.

summary.one_liner: A macOS/Windows companion app that reads AI provider usage limits through the local CodexBar CLI and streams them over USB serial to an ESP32 desk display (CYD or Guition ESP32-S3-4848S040).
keywords: see my ai quota at a glance
hardware status display for ai tools
summary.what_it_does: Runs on a Mac or Windows PC and periodically queries the locally installed CodexBar CLI for usage limits from Claude, ChatGPT, Antigravity, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, and Cursor. It sends a compact JSON frame over USB serial to an ESP32 board, which renders the limits on a small display with session, weekly, and provider-specific rows, live reset countdowns, and a local clock. The display can show up to eight windows that rotate or are switched by touch, plus a standby clock when the app is not running. The companion can flash firmware, check GitHub Releases for updates, and store per-device settings such as orientation, theme, brightness, and timezone. Experimental features include declarative display plugins and a Claude Code window that reports sessions waiting for approval or input via local HTTP hooks.
use_cases: glance at remaining Claude or ChatGPT usage while working
build a physical desk display for AI usage limits
flash ESP32 CYD firmware for a usage monitor
track Copilot premium request quota on a desk gadget
show Cursor or Gemini limits without keeping a browser tab open
get alerted when Claude Code sessions need input
how_to_run: Buy an ESP32-2432S028 (Cheap Yellow Display) or Guition ESP32-S3-4848S040 board
Install CodexBar so its local CLI is available
Download the AI Monitor Mac (app-v*) or Windows (win-v*) app from GitHub Releases
Plug the ESP32 into the computer with a USB data cable
Flash the matching firmware variant and choose a provider in the AI Monitor settings window
Build from source: cd companion && ./build.sh (Mac) or cd companion-windows && pnpm install && cargo tauri dev (Windows)
notable: Data stays on USB: the ESP32 needs no Wi-Fi and never receives cloud credentials, relying on the local CodexBar CLI as the data source
Intelligent window mode switches the display to whichever provider window has a meaningful usage change, threshold crossing, or reset
Declarative .aimplugin display plugins contain no executable code and are shown as unsigned before install
Mac app is signed with Developer ID and notarized; Windows app is a Tauri 2 build with a Rust backend
Supports both a 2.8in 320x240 CYD and a 4in 480x480 square ESP32-S3 board
caveats: Requires CodexBar installed and configured; the app does not talk to AI services directly
Requires macOS 14+ or Windows 10/11 x64, and a USB data cable (not charge-only)
Windows installer is not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen warns on first launch
Display plugins and the Claude Code window are marked as in development
Requires buying specific ESP32 hardware; some enclosures are third-party MakerWorld designs
